title: sirius-api — write path: contract → chromium
lede_html: Click any node — or a numbered beat below — to animate that step's flows; Ctrl/⌘-click adds more nodes to the selection; click again (or empty space) to release. Amber = retry (pre-drive failures only), red = non-retryable dead-letter, green = confirm. In e2e the only substitution is SmartID → the fake.
aria: Interactive system diagram of the sirius-api transfer write path
default_caption: Click a node to see how the code flows through it.

nodes.name: erp-adapter
nodes.caption: erp-adapter dual-writes: the snapshot store first, then sirius-api's contract route.

nodes.name: POST /transfers
nodes.caption: POST /transfers — erp-core's thin route calls whatever TransferWriter sirius-api injected; returns 202 + DocumentRef.

nodes.name: EnqueueingWriter
nodes.caption: EnqueueingWriter — persists the pending DocumentRef in Postgres, then publishes the WriteCommand. ADR 0006: no orphaned fiscal documents.

nodes.name: sirius_rpa_writes
nodes.caption: sirius_rpa_writes — durable queue, persistent JSON messages; retries re-enter here with a bumped attempt counter.

nodes.name: writes.dead
nodes.caption: writes.dead — the operator review queue: exhausted retries AND first-attempt non-retryable failures land here with a verify-first reason.

nodes.name: worker · consume
nodes.caption: worker · consume — prefetch 1, one chromium per process; each message: decode → handle → advance status → ack.

nodes.name: dispatch by resource
nodes.caption: dispatch by resource — transfers route to the nav pipeline; every other resource rides the generic testid writer.

nodes.name: generic writer
nodes.caption: generic writer — the natural-key-idempotent form flow every non-transfer resource uses.

nodes.name: TransferWriter
nodes.caption: TransferWriter — revalidates the payload into TransferCreate, maps store ids → SmartID store names, lines → import rows.

nodes.name: ArticleResolver
nodes.caption: ArticleResolver — read-through: the smartid_article_map cache answers first; a miss asks the public GenericApi by barcode and caches forever. Never guesses.

nodes.name: SmartID GenericApi
nodes.caption: SmartID GenericApi — GET …/snapshot_date/articole_rom_cb?barcode= · bare JSON array, empty = not found, multiple = refuse.

nodes.name: .xls → NavDriver
nodes.caption: .xls → NavDriver — writes ID_ARTICOL/CANTITATE/PRET and drives the frozen production nav scripts. Any failure past this point is NON-retryable.

nodes.name: SmartID UI
nodes.caption: SmartID UI — chromium drives the real screens; in e2e the fake serves the same ids and texts.

nodes.name: documents
nodes.caption: documents — the durable truth both processes share: pending → confirmed / dead_lettered; reconciliation re-drives overdue pending rows.

nodes.name: smartid_article_map
nodes.caption: smartid_article_map — product_id → id_articol, resolved once per product by barcode; alembic 0002, Postgres in prod, sqlite in tests.

beats.html: Contract route — erp-core's thin POST /transfers calls the injected writer.
Pending ref — durably pending in Postgres, then a WriteCommand publishes.
Broker — the durable queue holds the job; the app already returned 202.
Pickup — the worker consumes (prefetch 1, one chromium per process).
Dispatch — transfers to the nav pipeline; everything else to the generic writer.
Resolve — barcode → id_articol: cache first, public GenericApi on a miss.
Drive — the .xls is written; the production nav scripts drive SmartID.

extras_html: Failure policy: before the drive (validation, mapping, resolution) failures retry up to 5×. Once the drive started, any failure is non-retryable — dead-lettered on attempt 1 with a “the notice MAY already exist, verify in SmartID first” reason. Unresolvable or ambiguous barcodes also dead-letter: the RPA never guesses.
